# 1 Clement Chapter 34 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 34 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_034_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 34

**34:1** The good worker receives the bread of his labor with confidence; but the slothful and negligent one cannot look his employer in the face.

**34:2** It is therefore necessary that we be eager in doing good; for all things come from him.

**34:3** For he foretells us: "Behold, the Lord, and his reward is before his face, to render to each according to his work."

**34:4** He therefore exhorts those who believe in him with their whole heart not to be slothful or idle in any good work.

**34:5** Let our glory and confidence be in him; let us be subject to his will; let us consider the whole host of his angels, how they stand ready and minister to his will.

**34:6** For the scripture says: "Ten thousands of ten thousands stood before him, and thousands of thousands ministered to him, and they cried out: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; all creation is full of his glory."

**34:7** And so, gathered together in concord of conscience, let us cry out to him earnestly as from one mouth, that we may become partakers in his great and glorious promises.

**34:8** For it says: "Eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and it has not entered into the heart of man, the things which God has prepared for those who wait for him."

---

## Translator's Note

Chapter 34 grounds the call to good works in eschatological reward and communal worship. Three elements stand out: (1) The citation in v. 3 blends Isaiah 40:10 and 62:11 (cf. Revelation 22:12); (2) the Trisagion in v. 6 is Isaiah 6:3, here quoted in what appears to be an early liturgical form — the angels' song from the throne room becomes the model for congregational worship; (3) the Isaiah 64:4 / 1 Corinthians 2:9 citation in v. 8, here applied to eschatological promise rather than spiritual wisdom. The call to gather and cry out "from one mouth" (v. 7) suggests a liturgical Sitz im Leben for this section. "Lord of Hosts" renders *Kyrios Sabaoth* (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA) over EMET's "Lord of Sabaoth."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus translation, balancing literalness and clarity.*
